institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university first and foremost. Sciences Po offered a broad range of courses within the fields of humanitarian affairs, foreign policy, security studies etc. which greatly appealed to me. It didn't hurt that it is also a reputable university. Additionally, I thought it would be a great opportunity to improve my French while getting a chance to explore what cultural events and activities Paris has to offer.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, I have been very satisfied with my study abroad experience. Four out of five courses have been interesting, my professors have been knowledgeable and passionate about their subjects, and most of my fellow students have been prepared for class and willing to contribute to class discussions by asking relevant questions and sharing their thoughts, opinions, and insights. Moreover, it has been great living in Paris. It is an amazing city with so much to offer.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Rather easy. We received several emails with instructions before and after arrival in Paris. It was also possible to contact a help desk and/or an Erasmus coordinator with any additional questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I cannot recall what assistance I received, but I at least didn't feel like I had to figure everything out by myself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived in Cité Universitaire, which I can highly recommend. It was easy to follow their application procedure and I applied early on (which I believe is necessary). It is very popular, and I know several people whose application was eventually rejected.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Not anything specific since living on campus isn't an option anyway as far as I know.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Again, I can highly recommend applying to Cité Universitaire. It is located a bit outside of the city centre, but it is such a great community, there are a lot of events (both cultural, educational, and social), and rent is cheap for Paris.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: True to the stereotypical depiction of French bureaucracy, the registration process (including registration for courses) was unnecessarily complicated. But at least I was aware of the steps and knew what to do. The process could do with an overhaul though.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Again, I cannot recall all the steps. I remember the process as being rather time consuming and not something that could be completed in one go.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to contact a help desk and/or Erasmus coordinator who were able to assist with the registration process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not successful at all. I had a list of about 20 courses I was interested in and ended up with just one of them. This despite being ready the moment course registration opened. It was quite frustrating at the time, but luckily I ended up being satisfied with most of my courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look into which courses are offered well in advance and prepare a list of the ones you're interested in. Make sure there are no timetable clashes and prepare yourself for the likely possibility that you will still have to be flexible and sign up for other courses once course registration opens. Try to maintain a positive mindset. At PSIA it is possible to add/drop courses the first week of the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, I was very satisfied. I had one course I was really disappointed with, but my other four courses were all good, two of them being exceptionally great.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I attended M1 level courses and found the academic level similar to that of UCPH. However, I had to follow five courses (they are typically 6 ECTS each at PSIA), so the workload was significantly higher.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It differed from course to course so it's hard to make any general claims, although I'd say that on average the teaching style was quite similar to that of UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Economics of Conflict
Developing and Emerging Economies; The Main Issues
Politics of Transitional Justice in Latin America
The Making of Foreign Policy in Latin America
Preventive Diplomacy and Multilateral Conflict Management in Africa

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Making of Foreign Policy in Latin America and Preventive Diplomacy and Multilateral Conflict Management in Africa were both outstanding courses with very knowledgeable and passionate professors.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation was less expensive than I expected. Food on the other hand can be quite expensive, although cheap alternatives exist as well (e.g. lunch/dinner at CROUS).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of non-academic opportunities at Sciences Po (some of these obviously being affected by the pandemic at present).

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't recall since I didn't attend any of them (aside from 2-3 events with guest speakers).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Surely that depends on the individual. Look at the opportunities you have and give some of them a go if you feel so inclined.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I used nearly all my weekends in Paris. There is so much to see and do (museums, concerts, the restaurant scene, the nightlife, the architecture, markets etc.) – either with new friends or visitors from back home. I would however also recommend exploring different parts of France if you have the time.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just approach people from the get-go. Talk to other students in the break. Most are extremely friendly and open to go grab a beer or coffee after class depending on the time.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Parisians know how to spend their free time in optimal ways and the city is always buzzing with life. Make the most of it.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Start working on your midterms and final essays early. Otherwise, you will quickly become too overwhelmed.
2) Professors encourage you to reach out with any question you might have regarding the course or your assignments. It's highly recommendable to take them up on their offer.
3) Take your studies seriously but don't forget to enjoy your free time! You're in Paris. Take advantage of that.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The whole experience. Getting to live in Paris with interesting people from all over the world and attending a great university.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I was slightly overwhelmed with the workload at the end of the semester. It was frustrating having to study all the time without being able to take advantage of my last weeks in Paris. Therefore, I cannot stress this enough: start early on your final assignments.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
